title: Finite-Height Noise and Detection Laws for Prime Recovery from Riemann Zeros via the Zeta Echo Spectrum
content: The first N non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function define a spectral coherence CN(u) = |N−1Σ eiγₙu|², the survival probability of the uniformly aligned state under evolution in u = log x. By Landau's formula this coherence has echoes at u = log n exactly when n is a prime power. We turn this classical fact into a quantitative finite-height readout theory. Using the first 1000 zeros (γ1000 = 1419.42), the estimator Λ̂N(n) = −√n Re SN(log n)/(T/2π) recovers the von Mangoldt function Λ(n) with a noise level that follows σΛ(n) ≈ 0.675 n/(T/2π) (fitted exponent 0.999, bootstrap interval 0.95–1.06). Prime powers are separable from other integers (AUC ≥ 0.90) up to a limit X satisfying X/log X ≈ 0.97 T/2π, which corresponds to roughly log(T/2πe) zeros per readable prime and lies far beyond the naive resolution scale T/2π. The readout depends on the arithmetic positions of the zeros: the AUC is 0.997 for the zeta zeros and 0.50 ± 0.04 (Poisson) and 0.50 ± 0.05 (GUE) for surrogates of equal density. Errors in the ordinates attenuate the echo by an exact Debye–Waller factor exp(−δ²log²n/2). A smooth taper gives no consistent gain. All results are reproducible from one script.
